# Round 33 (cont.) — Correcting the record: the slack-constraint lemma, the `s = N^{1/6}` sieve target, a free sound pair filter, and a 145-module unread audit

**Supersedes/corrects** #417 (`FACT round-33 — THE ORDER-FREE OPENING IS CLOSED…`). The
adversarial gate caught errors in that paper and in the campaign record itself; this note
issues the corrections and the new rigorous facts. A kill is success; a caught error is
better than a retraction. Everything below was source-checked per Rule (5) — full texts
opened via `pdftotext`/HTML, Lean files read, numbers reproduced.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** on the deterministic record (never a floor). No
unconditional superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model.

---

## 1. ★ The slack-constraint lemma (a general screening test — headline)

> **Lemma (slack constraint).** A "hypothesis `X` fell, therefore the exponent moves"
> argument is valid only if `X`'s constraint is **active at the unconstrained optimum**.
> If at the optimum the constraint's ceiling strictly exceeds what the algorithm needs,
> the constraint is slack and the exponent cannot move, no matter that `X` fell.

**Application (this is the round's cleanest general result).** The record argued that
because the order-finding hypothesis (arXiv:2601.11131) fell, the `N^{1/5}` exponent might
drop. Re-derivation shows the constraint on `m` (Harvey's baby-step ceiling) had ceiling
`N^{2/5}` while the optimum needs only `N^{1/5}` — **slack by a factor `lg^{0.8}N`, growing
without bound**. A slack constraint cannot transmit a hypothesis-collapse to the exponent.
Harvey's own Prop 4.3 calls the order-finding step "negligible." The "opening" is closed
for a *general* reason, not an ad-hoc one.

This lemma is the reusable screening tool the campaign lacked: **before claiming a
structural change moves an exponent, check whether the relevant constraint is tight at the
optimum.** It retires a whole family of "something fell ⟹ something improves" arguments.

## 2. ★ The sieve target is 3× harder than the file (and than #417) says

> **Correction.** Including Prop 2.5's smoothness-sieve carrier, the pair-filter rate is
> `e = 1/5 − σ/5`, **not** `1/5 − 3σ/5`. Reaching `1/6` needs **`s = N^{1/6}`**, not
> `s = N^{1/18}`.

Both the campaign record and paper #417 stated the `N^{1/18}` target. That is wrong by 3×
in the exponent, because the dominant `lg^{16/5}` carrier is Prop 2.5's sieve, which a
pair filter does **not** divide. The single most concrete derived target in the record is
therefore three times harder than advertised. (The *pair-sweep* term does fall with `s` —
that part stands — but it is not the carrier.)

## 3. A free, sound, quantity-matched pair filter exists

> **Correction to a negative.** "No quantity-matched filter on Harvey's `(a,b)` family is
> known" is **false**: **keep iff `a ≤ b`** is sound and free (`s = 2` exactly), because
> Harvey's Lemma 3.3 (via Hardy–Wright) guarantees the good pair has `a ≤ b`. It buys
> `0.93×` — not an exponent — but it falsifies a stated negative and shows the filter
> space is not empty.

## 4. The two summands of Harvey's `s` are exactly equal (2× accounting correction)

Measured ratio `1.000000` across seven bit sizes: `s = 2·N^{1/5}lg^{1/5}N`, the two summands
exactly balanced. The record's "the `r`-term dominates" is wrong by 2×, and its "the
`s`-term is 100% of the leading term" is also wrong — the `m` (baby-step) term is
**co-dominant**. Combined with fact 1's "three co-leaders, two order-free," this settles
an accounting question the record twice admitted it could not.

## 5. Euler-gap density is governed by cofactors, not the gap

> **Correction.** Substituting `p−1 = ga`, `q−1 = gb`, the reveal density is
> `ρ = (a+b−2)/(ab)` — **the gap `g` cancels entirely**. So `Sup ρ = 1`, not `1/2`.

The "large-Euler-gap" framing over-credited `g`. The variable that matters is the
*cofactors* `a, b` (how `p−1, q−1` decompose), not the shared factor. The `O(1)`-base
`p−1`-style reveal remains real on its promise class, but the governing quantity is
misnamed in the record.

## 6. UMW's `1/6` is its floor with **zero slack** — and the one open door

- UMW's budget for a covering is `n^{2β+α} = n` against `θ(n) ~ n`; the ratio `→ 1`.
  There is **no slack** at `α = β = 1/3`: `1/6` is the **floor of UMW's framework**, not a
  reachable-but-unreached point. (The `3/2 → 4/3` *polynomial*-factorization consequence
  keeps its own slack; it is the integer-`1/6` consequence that is tight.)
- **The only formally-open door in the campaign**, per UMW Lemmas 6.2–6.3: all design
  freedom is in *"the choice of the factorization of `U`"*; the generic case is killed by
  counting. Concrete task: enumerate factorizations `U = U_1···U_ℓ` of the relevant smooth
  integer meeting Lemma 6.3's bounds, build the associated AP/GAP pair, and test whether
  `S − T` covers `[n]` by divisibility at `n = 10^4–10^6`, with **`S ∩ T = ∅` enforced**.
  Two guards (both earned by retractions this round): reject any candidate with
  `S ∩ T ≠ ∅` (the zero difference satisfies the `n`-divisor property free, giving spurious
  100% coverage), and treat coverage that *decreases* with `n` under a raised cap as a
  lower bound on achievability, not a measurement.

## 7. The 145-module unread audit (the campaign's real diagnosis)

> **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog modules were never read** by the 32 prior
> rounds. Two of the campaign's most decisive kills — the **non-abelian/braid** route and
> the **CM order-shadow** route — sat unread the entire time.

Three of round 33's twelve channels were re-derivations of theorems already sitting
unopened on disk. The campaign's failures are **failures of attention, not insight**. This
is the single most important measurement of the round and it sets the frontier: the next
rounds must read the unread surface before proposing anything.

## 8. Further theorem-worthy facts (barriers/corrections)

- **Attribution:** the `N^{1/3}` large-order-target conjecture is **Hittmeir's** (GFHP
  Remark 3.6 → [Hit18]), not Harvey's. (#417 got this right; restated for the record.)
- **GFHP Lemma 3.5 caveat:** `δ = N^{1/3}` **violates** the lemma's own precondition
  (`δ ≥ N^{1/4}log^8N`) for every `N ≥ 2^96`. So the "large-order element already
  published" claim holds only below a size threshold; for cryptographic `N` it does not
  apply as stated. (Corrects an overclaim in #417 §2.)
- **CM order-shadow:** the claimed linear class-number "0.75h penalty" is an **instrument
  artifact** — the harness took `Re(j)` of complex `j`, producing non-real-rooted
  polynomials with Galois group `S_h` instead of `Cl(D)`. With true polynomials the class
  number **cancels exactly**, *confirming* `Capstone.lean` (not correcting it).
- **Short-window ergodicity is false:** 126 of 429 primes refute full-period
  `log₂`-uniformity, because the orbit starts at the rational point `1/N`, a periodic
  orbit in the exceptional null set of an a.e. theorem. The short-window value-level
  result is therefore a **null with empty tail**, not a proof.
- **Effective-sample-size rule:** only **163 of 38,635** primes in `[2^19, 2^20)` have
  13-smooth `p−1`. Report distinct-prime counts, never draw counts, for any
  smoothness-labelled permutation test (a p-value here treated replicated primes as
  independent draws — a Rule (6) violation).
- **Berggren A-spine identity** `a_k − b_k = (−1)^{k+1}` collapses five proposed gcds to
  ~one event.

---

### Net effect on the campaign
- The flagship "order-free opening" is **closed** for a general reason (slack-constraint
  lemma, §1) — not merely "not yet achieved."
- The single concrete derived target, the `(a,b)` pair filter, is now correctly specified
  at **`s = N^{1/6}`** (§2) and is **not known to be impossible** (§3) but is worth `0.93×`
  as it stands.
- The one formally-open door is a **constructive UMW covering via primorial
  factorizations** (§6), and the largest unexplored surface is the **145 unread catalog
  modules** (§7).

**Next:** read the 145-module surface (especially the unread non-abelian/braid and CM
order-shadow kills), and run the UMW primorial-factorization covering search under the two
guards. Both are the honest frontier; everything else measured is a dead channel or a
correction now issued.

# FINAL CAMPAIGN REPORT — 33 papers, every factoring family closed, zero methods, a rigorous frontier

**The campaign's complete scientific conclusion.** Rounds 33–44 ran a gated pipeline
(hunt → refute ×2 distinct lenses → validated experiment → adversarial synthesis) and produced
**33 papers** (#417–#450, all `approved-direction`) plus 8 commits updating the record. This
note consolidates them into the single authoritative account.

## THE HEADLINE, STATED HONESTLY
> **Zero new factoring methods were found.** The deterministic `N^{1/5}` frontier is
> **unchanged** (`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a proven floor; no unconditional
> superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model). But **every route family is
> now closed by a theorem or a validated measurement**, the campaign's own record is corrected
> in place, and one **published external refutation** (He–Sahai, arXiv:2608.06681) was found,
> verified, and absorbed.

## WHAT WAS CLOSED, AND BY WHAT KIND OF ARGUMENT
| Family | Verdict | Kind of argument |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic `N^{1/5}` (Lehman–BSGS) | **motif-intrinsic** | 3 independent re-derivations: slack-constraint lemma; delete-a-term/closed-variable; add-a-floor/motif-exhaustion. Faithful model: interior + m-leg are **slack** |
| UMW divisor-cover (arXiv:2511.10851) | **1-D refuted** | **published theorem** (He–Sahai): false for `α<1/2, β<3/8`, in particular `(1/3,1/3)`; rank-2 remains open |
| Pythagorean / Berggren | **dead** | **theorem**: non-circular channel is a coordinate gcd; cost floor `Y^0.6232`; branching < entry-growth |
| Galois/Frobenius side-channels | **closed 3 ways** | abelianization cap, exact which-factor wall, torsor no-pruning (a machine-checked **fifth-primitive ghost**) |
| Smoothness | **deep + orthogonal** | no per-instance upper bound; the `N^{1/5}` record carries **no smoothness term** |
| Transcendence (Baker/S-unit) | **closed** | object mismatch — Matveev never sees `N` |
| Class-group route | **priced by ERH, not Cohen–Lenstra** | family→subfamily transfer **measured false** (`z=−41.4`); `h(−pq)` is output, not cost |
| Quadratic sieve (QS) | **no-decoupling is a theorem** | column space = split set; complete-cost rule inverts the sieve-only sign |
| NFS | **as closed as QS** | column set decoupled from `N` (governed by `d`) but **no exploitable excess** |

1. **The slack-constraint lemma** (general): a falling hypothesis moves an exponent only if
   its constraint is **active** at the unconstrained optimum (round 33; killed the
   order-finding "opening").
2. **The complete-cost rule** (general): price the **complete** cost — sieve **plus** GF(2)
   elimination — not the sieve alone; pricing sieve-only **inverts the sign** of the `Q`-slope
   (round 43; corrected round 42 and my own #445).
3. **The inequality-direction rule** (general): a proved ceiling can price the wrong side
   (`rank+1 ≤ k_success` runs backwards ⇒ a rank ceiling is not a work bound; round 42).
4. **The vacuity filter** (general): any exponential-in-`|S|`/rank bound must beat the trivial
   bound (the ECM-point published bound was 7.3×10⁵ orders worse than doing nothing; round 39).
5. **The generator-population ban**: never pool over instances and report a within-pool SE as
   a z-score (round 40).
6. **Symmetric-readout vacuity** (general): for an unordered secret and an order-sensitive
   label, every public-input readout is blind (round 33/34).
7. **He–Sahai's published refutation** of the UMW AP door (found, verified, absorbed).

- The record's **"density barrier is absolute … for any method"** was downgraded to
  **conjectured-absolute** (its necessary ingredient does not exist).
- The record's **`2-torsion = C₂` for every N** is false for `N≡1 (mod 4)`.
- The record's **`~1/4` multi-poly column set** was `0.487–0.505` (same as single-poly).
- The record's **`k_success ≤ Q+1`** is not a theorem; and `rank+1 ≤ k_success` (backwards).
- **My own posts were corrected**: #445 (oracle prize struck), #446 (`~1/4` wrong), **#449
  RETRACTED** (posted raw logs before adversarial verification — both numbers struck on
  unreproducibility and truncation).
- The campaign's own failures were diagnosed as **attention, not insight** (145 of 185 modules
  unread; 4 retractions from unread material) — and the fix was enforced structurally.

## THE EXACT OPEN DOORS (the honest frontier)
1. **UMW rank-2 additive separability** — realize `n^{2/3}` of prime mass as the difference
   set of two `n^{1/3}`-sets, overdetermined by `n^{1/3}`; no construction found.
2. **The smooth-value upper bound for structured forms** (`Ψ_F ≤ C·x·∏ρ(d_i u)`) — the
   smoothness-escape horn's missing ingredient, open in both directions.
3. **A per-instance class-number bound** for a single `Q(√(−pq))` — the class-group lever,
   currently unreachable by enumeration.

**The campaign's contribution is a rigorous, self-correcting negative result with a
precisely-characterised frontier — not a factoring method.** That is the honest outcome, and
it is the one the evidence supports.

/-!
# The multi-polynomial column set *is* the single-polynomial split set

The campaign record once claimed that the multiple-polynomial quadratic sieve
(MPQS) confines relations to a column set of density `~1/4` of the factor base,
half of the single-polynomial density.  The measured density was `0.487–0.505`,
i.e. the same `1/2`.  This file proves why: **changing the polynomial cannot
change the column set.**

The single-polynomial facts live in `Catalog.Shared.QSRelationPoolRandom`
(`QSRelationPool.qsValue`, `exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare`,
`card_admissible_residues`).  Here we add:

* `mpqsValue N a b x = (a x + b)^2 - N`, the shifted/scaled sieve polynomial, and
  `mpqsReduced a b c x = a x^2 + 2 b x + c` with `b^2 - a c = N`, the actual
  MPQS polynomial (`a · Q(x) = (a x + b)^2 - N`).
* `exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare`, `exists_dvd_mpqsReduced_iff_isSquare`:
  for every prime `p ∤ a`, `p` divides *some* value of the polynomial iff `N` is
  a square mod `p` — exactly the single-polynomial criterion.
* `family_columns_iff`: for an arbitrary (nonempty) family of polynomials, the
  union of their column sets, restricted to primes coprime to all leading
  coefficients, is precisely the split set.  No family enlarges or shrinks it.
* `mpqs_column_density`: the number of residues `N mod p` for which `p` is a
  column of a given MPQS polynomial is exactly `(p-1)/2`: density `1/2`, not
  `1/4`.
-/

namespace FactoringFrontier.MultiPoly

open QSRelationPool

/-- The scaled-and-shifted sieve polynomial `(a x + b)^2 - N`. -/
def mpqsValue (N a b x : ℤ) : ℤ := (a * x + b) ^ 2 - N

/-- The reduced MPQS polynomial `a x^2 + 2 b x + c`. -/
def mpqsReduced (a b c x : ℤ) : ℤ := a * x ^ 2 + 2 * b * x + c

/-- The MPQS identity: if `b^2 - a c = N` then `a · Q(x) = (a x + b)^2 - N`. -/
theorem mpqsReduced_scale {N a b c : ℤ} (hN : b ^ 2 - a * c = N) (x : ℤ) :
    a * mpqsReduced a b c x = mpqsValue N a b x := by
  unfold mpqsReduced mpqsValue
  rw [← hN]; ring

/-- `mpqsValue` is the single-polynomial value at the shifted point `a x + b`. -/
theorem mpqsValue_eq_qsValue (N a b x : ℤ) : mpqsValue N a b x = qsValue N (a * x + b) := rfl

/-- **Multi-polynomial column criterion.**  For a prime `p` not dividing the
leading coefficient `a`, the prime `p` divides some value `(a x + b)^2 - N` iff
`N` is a quadratic residue mod `p`. -/
theorem exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ}
    (ha : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) (N b : ℤ) :
    (∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsValue N a b x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    exact isSquare_of_dvd_qsValue (x := a * x + b) hx
  · intro hsq
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare (p := p) N).2 hsq
    -- solve `a x + b ≡ y (mod p)` using that `a` is a unit mod `p`
    have ha' : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := by
      rwa [Ne, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
    set x0 : ZMod p := (a : ZMod p)⁻¹ * ((y : ZMod p) - b)
    refine ⟨(x0.val : ℤ), ?_⟩
    rw [mpqsValue_eq_qsValue, dvd_qsValue_iff_sq_eq]
    rw [dvd_qsValue_iff_sq_eq] at hy
    have hx0 : ((x0.val : ℕ) : ZMod p) = x0 := ZMod.natCast_zmod_val x0
    push_cast
    rw [hx0]
    have : (a : ZMod p) * x0 + b = y := by
      simp only [x0]; field_simp; ring
    rw [this, hy]

/-- **Reduced MPQS column criterion.**  With `b^2 - a c = N` and `p ∤ a`, the
prime `p` divides some value of `a x^2 + 2 b x + c` iff `N` is a square mod `p`. -/
theorem exists_dvd_mpqsReduced_iff_isSquare {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {N a b c : ℤ}
    (hN : b ^ 2 - a * c = N) (ha : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) :
    (∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsReduced a b c x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by
  rw [← exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare ha N b]
  have hpr : Prime (p : ℤ) := Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.mp hp.out
  refine exists_congr fun x => ?_
  rw [← mpqsReduced_scale hN x]
  constructor
  · intro h; exact Dvd.dvd.mul_left h a
  · intro h
    rcases hpr.dvd_or_dvd h with h' | h'
    · exact absurd h' ha
    · exact h'

/-- **No polynomial family changes the column set.**  For any nonempty family of
shifted sieve polynomials `(a_i x + b_i)^2 - N` and any prime `p` coprime to all
leading coefficients, `p` is a column of *some* member of the family iff it is
in the single-polynomial split set (`N` a square mod `p`). -/
theorem family_columns_iff {ι : Type*} [Nonempty ι] (A B : ι → ℤ) {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hA : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ A i) (N : ℤ) :
    (∃ i, ∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ mpqsValue N (A i) (B i) x) ↔ IsSquare (N : ZMod p) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, h⟩
    exact (exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare (hA i) N (B i)).1 h
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty ι›
    exact ⟨i, (exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare (hA i) N (B i)).2 h⟩

open Classical in
/-- **Column density is `1/2`, not `1/4`.**  For an odd prime `p` and a fixed
leading coefficient `a` with `p ∤ a`, the set of nonzero residues `n mod p` for

   for every prime `ℓ ≤ m` the residue classes of `A` and of `B` modulo `ℓ` are
   *disjoint*, hence `#(A mod ℓ) + #(B mod ℓ) ≤ ℓ`.
   `parity_rigidity` is the case `ℓ = 2`: all of `A` has one parity, all of `B`
   the other.

These are the admissibility (sieve-dimension) constraints of the rank-2 problem:
a construction must live in a product of residue-class boxes avoiding the
diagonal at every small prime, *and* be injective.

namespace FactoringFrontier.RankTwo

open Finset

/-- `(A, B)` is a prime-difference pair above `m`: every difference `a - b` is,
in absolute value, a prime exceeding `m`. -/
def PrimeDiffPair (A B : Finset ℤ) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, (a - b).natAbs.Prime ∧ m < (a - b).natAbs

/-- A prime difference exceeding `m ≥ ℓ` cannot be divisible by the prime `ℓ`. -/
theorem residues_ne_of_primeDiff {ℓ m : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hm : ℓ ≤ m) {a b : ℤ}
    (h : (a - b).natAbs.Prime ∧ m < (a - b).natAbs) : (a : ZMod ℓ) ≠ (b : ZMod ℓ) := by
  intro hab
  have hdvd : (ℓ : ℤ) ∣ a - b := by
    rw [← ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
    push_cast
    rw [hab, sub_self]
  have h2 : ℓ ∣ (a - b).natAbs := Int.ofNat_dvd_left.1 hdvd
  have := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hℓ h.1).1 h2
  omega

/-- **Residue classes are disjoint.**  For a prime-difference pair above `m`
and any prime `ℓ ≤ m`, `A` and `B` occupy disjoint residue classes mod `ℓ`. -/
theorem residue_classes_disjoint {A B : Finset ℤ} {m ℓ : ℕ} (hAB : PrimeDiffPair A B m)
    (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hm : ℓ ≤ m) :
    Disjoint (A.image (fun a : ℤ => (a : ZMod ℓ))) (B.image (fun b : ℤ => (b : ZMod ℓ))) := by
  rw [disjoint_left]
  intro r hrA hrB
  obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 hrA
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hba⟩ := mem_image.1 hrB
  exact residues_ne_of_primeDiff hℓ hm (hAB a ha b hb) hba.symm

/-- **Local residue budget.**  `#(A mod ℓ) + #(B mod ℓ) ≤ ℓ` for every prime
`ℓ ≤ m`. -/
theorem residue_budget {A B : Finset ℤ} {m ℓ : ℕ} (hAB : PrimeDiffPair A B m)
    (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hm : ℓ ≤ m) :
    (A.image (fun a : ℤ => (a : ZMod ℓ))).card + (B.image (fun b : ℤ => (b : ZMod ℓ))).card
      ≤ ℓ := by
  haveI : NeZero ℓ := ⟨hℓ.ne_zero⟩
  rw [← card_union_of_disjoint (residue_classes_disjoint hAB hℓ hm)]
  calc _ ≤ (univ : Finset (ZMod ℓ)).card := card_le_univ _
    _ = ℓ := by rw [card_univ, ZMod.card]

/-- **Parity rigidity (`ℓ = 2`).**  If `B` is nonempty and `(A, B)` is a
prime-difference pair above `m ≥ 2`, then any two elements of `A` have the same
parity. -/
theorem parity_rigidity {A B : Finset ℤ} {m : ℕ} (hAB : PrimeDiffPair A B m) (hm : 2 ≤ m)
    (hB : B.Nonempty) {a a' : ℤ} (ha : a ∈ A) (ha' : a' ∈ A) : Even (a - a') := by
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hB
  have h1 := residues_ne_of_primeDiff Nat.prime_two hm (hAB a ha b hb)
  have h2 := residues_ne_of_primeDiff Nat.prime_two hm (hAB a' ha' b hb)
  -- in `ZMod 2`, two elements different from the same `b` are equal
  have key : (a : ZMod 2) = (a' : ZMod 2) := by
    revert h1 h2
    generalize (a : ZMod 2) = x
    generalize (a' : ZMod 2) = y
    generalize (b : ZMod 2) = z
    revert x y z
    decide
  have : ((a - a' : ℤ) : ZMod 2) = 0 := by push_cast; rw [key, sub_self]
  rw [ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] at this
  exact even_iff_two_dvd.2 (by exact_mod_cast this)

/-- **Capacity: no slack.**  If every element of `T` is an absolute difference
`|a - b|` with `a ∈ A`, `b ∈ B`, then `|T| ≤ |A|·|B|`. -/
theorem prime_cover_capacity (A B : Finset ℤ) (T : Finset ℕ)
    (hT : ∀ t ∈ T, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, (a - b).natAbs = t) :
    T.card ≤ A.card * B.card := by

    intro t ht

/-!
# Symmetric-readout vacuity and the exact `1/2` which-factor wall

Standing finding 6 of the campaign ("for an unordered secret and an
order-sensitive label, every public-input readout is blind") and the
"exact which-factor wall" of the Galois side-channel closure are made precise
here as a *counting* theorem, with an attaining decoder.

Setting: a finite secret set `S`, an involution `σ` of `S` (e.g. swapping the
two prime factors), a public readout `R` with `R ∘ σ = R` (e.g. `N = p·q`), and
a label `L` with `L (σ x) ≠ L x` (e.g. "the first factor").

* `which_factor_wall`: **every** decoder `D` is correct on at most half of `S`:
  `2 · #{x ∈ S | D (R x) = L x} ≤ #S`.
* `symmetric_readout_vacuity`: in particular no decoder is correct on all of a
  nonempty `S`.
* `semiprime_which_factor_wall`: the instance `S = ` ordered pairs of distinct
  primes from a finite set `P`, `R (p,q) = p q`, `L (p,q) = p`.
* `minFac_attains_wall`: the decoder `N ↦ N.minFac` is correct on **exactly**
  half of `S`, so the wall `1/2` is sharp.
-/

namespace FactoringFrontier.WhichFactor

open Finset

section Abstract

variable {X Y Z : Type*} [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Z]

/-- **The which-factor wall.**  Under a readout invariant under an involution
that flips the label, any decoder succeeds on at most half of the secrets. -/
theorem which_factor_wall (S : Finset X) (σ : X → X) (hσS : ∀ x ∈ S, σ x ∈ S)
    (hinv : ∀ x, σ (σ x) = x) (R : X → Y) (hR : ∀ x, R (σ x) = R x)
    (L : X → Z) (hL : ∀ x ∈ S, L (σ x) ≠ L x) (D : Y → Z) :
    2 * (S.filter (fun x => D (R x) = L x)).card ≤ S.card := by
  set T := S.filter (fun x => D (R x) = L x) with hT
  have hinj : Set.InjOn σ (T : Set X) := fun x _ y _ hxy => by
    rw [← hinv x, ← hinv y, hxy]
  have himg_card : (T.image σ).card = T.card := card_image_of_injOn hinj
  have hdisj : Disjoint T (T.image σ) := by
    rw [disjoint_left]
    intro x hxT hxI
    obtain ⟨y, hyT, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 hxI
    have hy := (mem_filter.1 hyT)
    have hx := (mem_filter.1 hxT)
    -- `D (R (σ y)) = D (R y) = L y`, but also `= L (σ y)`
    apply hL y hy.1
    rw [← hx.2, hR, hy.2]
  have hsub : T ∪ T.image σ ⊆ S := by
    intro x hx
    rcases mem_union.1 hx with h | h
    · exact (mem_filter.1 h).1
    · obtain ⟨y, hyT, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 h
      exact hσS y (mem_filter.1 hyT).1
  have := card_le_card hsub
  rw [card_union_of_disjoint hdisj, himg_card] at this
  omega

/-- **Symmetric-readout vacuity.**  On a nonempty secret set, no decoder of a
symmetric readout recovers an order-sensitive label everywhere. -/
theorem symmetric_readout_vacuity (S : Finset X) (hS : S.Nonempty) (σ : X → X)
    (hσS : ∀ x ∈ S, σ x ∈ S) (hinv : ∀ x, σ (σ x) = x) (R : X → Y)
    (hR : ∀ x, R (σ x) = R x) (L : X → Z) (hL : ∀ x ∈ S, L (σ x) ≠ L x) (D : Y → Z) :
    ¬ ∀ x ∈ S, D (R x) = L x := by
  intro hall
  have hw := which_factor_wall S σ hσS hinv R hR L hL D
  rw [filter_true_of_mem hall] at hw
  have := hS.card_pos
  omega

end Abstract

section Semiprime

/-- Ordered pairs of distinct elements of `P`. -/
def orderedPairs (P : Finset ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) := P.offDiag

/-- **Semiprime which-factor wall.**  For any decoder `D : ℕ → ℕ`, the number of
ordered pairs `(p, q)` of distinct elements of `P` with `D (p q) = p` is at most
half the number of pairs. -/
theorem semiprime_which_factor_wall (P : Finset ℕ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) :
    2 * ((orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => D (x.1 * x.2) = x.1)).card
      ≤ (orderedPairs P).card := by
  refine which_factor_wall (orderedPairs P) Prod.swap ?_ (fun x => Prod.swap_swap x)
    (fun x => x.1 * x.2) (fun x => Nat.mul_comm _ _) Prod.fst ?_ D
  · intro x hx
    simp only [orderedPairs, mem_offDiag] at hx ⊢
    exact ⟨hx.2.1, hx.1, fun h => hx.2.2 h.symm⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp only [orderedPairs, mem_offDiag] at hx
    exact fun h => hx.2.2 h.symm

/-- The ordered pairs split evenly into increasing and decreasing ones. -/
theorem two_mul_card_lt_pairs (P : Finset ℕ) :
    2 * ((orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => x.1 < x.2)).card = (orderedPairs P).card := by
  set U := (orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => x.1 < x.2)
  set W := (orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => ¬ x.1 < x.2)
  have hsplit := card_filter_add_card_filter_not
    (s := orderedPairs P) (fun x : ℕ × ℕ => x.1 < x.2)
  have hW : W = U.image Prod.swap := by
    ext x
    simp only [W, U, orderedPairs, mem_filter, mem_offDiag, mem_image]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨h1, h2, h3⟩, h4⟩
      refine ⟨x.swap, ⟨⟨h2, h1, fun h => h3 h.symm⟩, ?_⟩, Prod.swap_swap x⟩
      simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
      omega
    · rintro ⟨y, ⟨⟨h1, h2, h3⟩, h4⟩, rfl⟩
      simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
      exact ⟨⟨h2, h1, fun h => h3 h.symm⟩, by omega⟩
  have hWc : W.card = U.card := by
    rw [hW]; exact card_image_of_injective _ Prod.swap_injective
  change U.card + W.card = _ at hsplit
  omega

/-- **The wall is sharp.**  If `P` consists of primes, the decoder
`N ↦ N.minFac` is correct on exactly half of the ordered pairs. -/
theorem minFac_attains_wall (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) :
    2 * ((orderedPairs P).filter (fun x => (x.1 * x.2).minFac = x.1)).card
      = (orderedPairs P).card := by
  rw [← two_mul_card_lt_pairs P]
  congr 2
  apply filter_congr
  intro x hx
  simp only [orderedPairs, mem_offDiag] at hx
  obtain ⟨hp, hq, hne⟩ := hx
  have hpP := hP _ hp
  have hqP := hP _ hq
  -- the least prime factor of `p q` is `min p q`
  have hmin : (x.1 * x.2).minFac = min x.1 x.2 := by
    have hdvd : (x.1 * x.2).minFac ∣ x.1 * x.2 := Nat.minFac_dvd _
    have hpr : (x.1 * x.2).minFac.Prime :=
      Nat.minFac_prime (by nlinarith [hpP.two_le, hqP.two_le] : 1 < x.1 * x.2).ne'
    rcases (Nat.Prime.dvd_mul hpr).1 hdvd with h | h
    · have e1 := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hpr hpP).1 h

    · have e1 := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hpr hqP).1 h

        Nat.minFac_le_of_dvd hpP.two_le (Dvd.intro _ rfl)
      rw [e1] at le2 ⊢; exact (min_eq_right le2).symm

`|A|·|B| ≤ C · X^2 / (log X)^2` for `A, B ⊂ [1, X]`. The `n^{2/3}`-from-`n^{1/3}`
rank-2 door therefore cannot be reached with `|A| = |B| = n^{1/3}` inside an
interval of length `n^{1/3+o(1)}`.
The key insight is that `residue_budget` gives a product of local densities
`∏_{ℓ≤m}(1 − ω_ℓ/ℓ)`, the setting of a two-dimensional Selberg sieve.
Why now? The local obstruction is now a theorem, so only the global sieve step
remains.

## 2. Exact leg-triple count as a divisor function
**Conjecture.** For odd `N`, the number of triples `N² + b² = c²` with `b > 0` is
exactly `(τ(N²) − 1)/2`. The number with `gcd(c−b, N) = 1` is always exactly one.
The key insight is that `leg_factor_identity` turns triples into ordered
factorisations `u·v = N²` with `u < v`, and for odd `N` the parity condition is automatic.
Why now? Both directions of the bijection are already in Lean.

## 3. Which-factor wall for k-factor secrets
**Conjecture.** For secrets that are ordered `k`-tuples of distinct primes,
readout = product, and label = the first coordinate, every decoder is correct on
at most a `1/k` fraction. `minFac` attains exactly `1/k`.
The key insight is that the symmetric group `S_k` acts freely on these tuples
while preserving the readout, so the involution argument becomes an orbit argument.
Why now? The `k = 2` case (`which_factor_wall`) is proved with an attaining
decoder.

The key insight is the same unit-shift argument as `exists_dvd_mpqsValue_iff_isSquare`,
applied to a root of `f` instead of a square root of `N`.
